maria (Support): Hey @raj — saw your ticket about the streaming response cutting off and causing a JSON parse error on your side. Can you paste the exact truncated output and the request-id if you have it? Also curious if you saw any 429/401/502 before the cutoff.

raj (Customer): Thanks Maria. Repro steps below. This is a streaming SSE call to /v1/generate that starts fine but the client gets a partial final JSON and no finish_reason. App expects a final chunk and fails. No 401s or 429s in our logs. Token is valid. Request id in our logs: rid=ab12cd34. Example curl we used:

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-x","prompt":"summarize...","stream":true}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

Truncated last lines we received (redacted):

```
event: data
data: {"id":"tok_...","delta":"text","role":"assistant","content":"...the final sentence continues but then abruptly stops"
event: data
data: {"id":"tok_...","delta":"text","content":"","finish_reason":
```

And then the connection closes from client side (socket EOF). No explicit [DONE] or a final JSON with finish_reason=null.

maria (Support): Thanks — that matches the "missing final chunk / finish_reason absent" pattern. Two quick asks while we triage: (1) can you share the raw bytes (hex or base64) of the last ~2KB so we can see if there's a partial UTF-8 sequence or cut inside a JSON token, and (2) are you going through any proxy/load-balancer (eg. nginx, envoy, Cloud LB)? Those often buffer or enforce idle timeouts.

raj (Customer): Pasted last 1.5KB (base64) into the ticket. We are behind an nginx reverse proxy (GCP LB -> nginx -> app). Nginx config has `proxy_read_timeout 60s` currently.

deploy-bot: deploy finished for release/2026-03-15-34 (sha: a1b2c3) to staging at 2026-03-15T14:06:00Z.

oliver (SRE): Chiming in — common culprits: proxy buffering, proxy read/idle timeouts, or the gateway resetting the upstream connection (RST_STREAM). If the client reconnects quickly and the runtime doesn't support resume, the model process may have been interrupted and never emitted a final 'finish_reason' event. From the rid ab12cd34 in our logs I see the runtime returned a 200 with chunked transfer until ~+55s then an upstream RST from the edge gateway. No 429 for that rid.

emily (Eng): I pulled the runtime traces for rid=ab12cd34. Observations: tokens emitted continuously until a partial token emission at 55s, then an upstream connection reset (RST) between the load-balancer and our serving runtime. The runtime's tokenizer state shows the generation completed, but the last flush to the socket was incomplete — likely an abrupt TCP FIN or proxy buffer flush. We don't show any internal model error flags.

maria (Support): Ok actionable items and mitigations: 
- Short term (customer): Implement client-side detection for partial final chunk and fallback to a non-streaming call (stream=false) for that request id. That lets you get a stable JSON response even if streaming fails.
- Near term: try disabling response buffering and increase idle timeouts in nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 180s; proxy_send_timeout 180s;` Also ensure `chunked_transfer_encoding on` and `Connection: keep-alive` between LB and nginx.
- Engineering / SRE: we need to confirm whether edge LB enforces a 60s idle close or issues RST on slow final flushes, and whether our runtime attempts to retry socket writes on transient EPIPE.

raj (Customer): We can patch nginx to increase timeouts and disable buffering. Curious — could a rotated auth token midstream cause this? We did rotate keys earlier in the day but the token used for this test was freshly minted.

oliver (SRE): Rotating auth shouldn't abruptly cut an existing TCP stream mid-request — the server will finish serving in-flight requests using the token presented at request start. More likely LB/keepalive settings. Also double-check for intermediate HTTP/2 termination — we've seen RST_STREAM on HTTP/2 proxies when the proxy thinks the request is idle.

emily (Eng): From runtime side, action plan: 
1) Add additional logging for socket-level errors (EPIPE/EINVAL) and log last emitted chunk boundary for better forensic data.
2) Add a short-lived feature flag to attempt a best-effort flush/retry if the write fails during the final flush (but only for non-idempotent operations if safe).
3) Validate our SSE framing: ensure each `data:` event is newline-terminated and we emit a final `data: {"finish_reason": "stop"}\n\n` or the equivalent final event.

maria (Support): For immediate repro we asked the customer to: 
- Apply nginx edits (proxy_buffering off + timeouts 180s), and retry the same curl.
- If still repros, capture tcpdump on the nginx host for the connection to the runtime for the request window.
- Send us the raw tcpdump and the base64 of last bytes.

raj (Customer): Will try the nginx change now. One more question — is there a way to resume without losing tokens if a reconnect happens? Our app wants to avoid duplication.

emily (Eng): We currently don't support an out-of-the-box byte-offset resume for SSE streams. Best patterns: 
- Use idempotent prompts or an application-level chunk-id you include in the prompt so you can dedupe on reconnect.
- For critical flows, do non-streaming finalization (a follow-up request that asks the model to emit the completed JSON when streaming detected as incomplete).

oliver (SRE): Quick checklist for customers: 
- Ensure there are no intermediate proxies with small `proxy_read_timeout` / `idle_timeout`. 
- Turn off response buffering at proxy tier. 
- Avoid HTTP/2 midstream termination if possible — test using direct HTTP/1.1 connection to see if behaviour changes.

maria (Support): Emily / Oliver — can you take the rid ab12cd34 and add socket-level traces + copy of edge LB config by EOD? Tagging @emily and @oliver. I'll keep the customer posted.

emily (Eng): Taking it. I'll attach the runtime trace and a suggested fix for final-flush retry tomorrow.

oliver (SRE): I'll pull the LB access logs and check for RST/timeout correlation.

raj (Customer): nginx changes applied (disabled buffering, timeouts 180s). Retried and the stream completed normally. Thanks everyone — looks like the proxy was the culprit. We'll keep the non-stream fallback in place while you roll the runtime improvements. :thumbsup:

maria (Support): Great — closing loop with customer. I'll keep this thread open until eng confirms runtime mitigations. Thanks team.
